maya: Quick heads-up: while running client-side benchmarks for the runtime changes (kernel selection + batching heuristics + KV cache tweaks) I see synthetic load showing much better p95 than our replay harness. Anyone else?

samir: yup, saw similar. My guess is client-side behavior — are you using connection pooling/keepalive?

maya: I was using hey with 200 concurrent connections, no explicit pooling. TLS for each request.

jess: that's the usual culprit. New TCP/TLS handshakes per request kill latency. Use HTTP keepalive or HTTP/2. We saw 25-40% worse p95 without pooling.

liam: also check TCP_NODELAY vs Nagle — small request bodies get delayed if Nagle on. For low-latency RPCs set TCP_NODELAY.

olga: and apples-to-apples: gRPC keeps a single channel so it avoids both HTTP handshake + TLS overhead. If you're comparing REST vs gRPC make both use persistent connections.

samir: another big one — KV cache warmup. Replay harness that doesn't re-use session ids produces cold KV hits; kernels selected for cold vs warm differ (KV cache affects sequence length and cache hits)

jess: profiling showed kernel-selector flips to larger-window kernels when batch shapes vary; synthetic traffic with fixed seq len underestimates kernel switch overhead. Need to mirror batch shape distribution.

opsbot: :rotating_light: perf-regression-alert: nightly-agent detected throughput -12% vs baseline after batching-heuristics rollout

maya: proposed action items:
1) update client harness to use connection pooling + keepalive
2) replay with session-affinity (persist user ids) so KV cache warms properly
3) enable TLS handshakes in synthetic harness (or reuse TLS contexts)
4) collect tcpdump + perf traces (CPU/kernels + nvprof) for failing runs

liam: quick snippets:
```
# curl keepalive example
curl --http1.1 --keepalive-time 60 -H "Connection: keep-alive" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate

# hey loadgen with persistent connections
hey -c 50 -q 10 -z 60s -H "Connection: keep-alive" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

jess: for replay harness: ensure same ordering and timing jitter, and add an instrumentation flag to record raw socket RTT/TLS handshake times.

olga: note on kernel selection: if you change quantization or int8 kernels, benchmark both warm and cold KV states. We had a regression where kernel switch cost was hidden in synthetic runs.

maya: thanks — I'll update the harness and re-run. Will post p95/p99 numbers + traces when done :thumbsup:
